summary: This step tests the Track 2 drug directions against sources that share nothing. E1 scored every possible BubR1 substitution for stability: the child's missense is predicted destabilising (87th percentile, pseudokinase domain), but eight published alleles are too few to validate the unstable-versus-inactive split. E2 matched the child's eight clinical terms against all 76,699 MGI mouse genotypes: a Bub1b mouse ranks in the top 1.0-1.4%, and its published interventions open a senolytic and mTOR direction (D5). E4 replicated the leads in PRISM (6,790 compounds, 919 lines): the statin direction reproduces weakly and survives no correction, chloroquine does not reproduce, and dasatinib is the 99.4th percentile on aneuploidy. E5+E6 asked whether each candidate is safe for this child from his genome and his phenotypes: only 1.6% of pharmacogene positions are callable and every guideline gene for a shortlisted drug is a no call, while 60.0% of candidates carry a label effect matching his own phenotypes against 39.7% in a matched set. Each experiment writes a submission note the final report is assembled from.
why: The iteration-2 Track 2 report rests its deepest lead (raise BubR1) on one mouse paper, and step 8 left the mechanism question open: a fold cannot say whether the weakened copy is unstable or inactive. Published MVA alleles split into exactly those two classes, and the mouse allelic series carries the tested interventions, so both questions are answerable from public data.
verdict: Eight claims settled or bounded. H083 refuted (stability cannot separate the two allele classes, AUROC 0.60, no power). H084 supported weakly (0.55). H085 supported (0.70, top 1.0-1.4% of mouse genotypes). H086 undecided (0.45, the two rollups disagree). H087 supported weakly (0.55: the statin direction reproduces, nothing survives correction, and the rank-1 molecule is untestable). H088 refuted (0.20: chloroquine shows no aneuploidy trend at p 0.315). H089 supported (0.80: the mixed D5 result is reported in both directions). H090 supported at low confidence (0.40: met literally by CYP3A5, unanswered for every gene that governs a shortlisted drug). H091 supported (0.70: 60.0% versus 39.7%, intervals non-overlapping, both positive controls recovered).

inherits.what: Step 7's PrimeKG walk and decoy control, step 8's Boltz-2 fold (entry 147) and GPU tier on Modal, and iteration 2's Track 2 directions D1 to D4, evidence ladder and do-not table.

hands_to.what: A Track 2 submission assembled from the per-experiment submission notes in docs/iteration4/step-9/submission-notes/, plus a list of corrections the iteration-2 report owes (collected in the step README) and one concrete clinical action: a targeted pharmacogenomic panel over the genes the delivered callset cannot read.

figures.name: step9-e1-atlas.svg
figures.reads: Mean ThermoMPNN ΔΔG of the 19 substitutions at each BubR1 residue along the protein, with UniProt domains; the folded TPR and pseudokinase domains run high and the disordered middle near zero. The published MVA alleles are marked by class (red = abundance-lowering, blue = stable). The child's allele is not marked on the position axis.
figures.means: High-ΔΔG alleles of both classes sit in the two folded domains, so position and stability alone cannot tell an unstable allele from an inactive one. That is why H083 fails.

figures.name: step9-e1-distribution.svg
figures.reads: The distribution of ΔΔG over all 19,950 possible substitutions, with the child's missense as one line at the 87th percentile.
figures.means: The child's substitution is more destabilising than most possible changes. That supports, weakly, the abundance-lowering reading that direction D3 needs.

figures.name: step9-e1-roc.svg
figures.reads: ROC of ΔΔG separating 5 abundance-lowering from 3 stable published MVA alleles: AUROC 0.60 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.13-1.00); the extended set with one non-MVA stable allele gives 0.70.
figures.means: With eight labels the curve cannot distinguish a useful score from chance. The test had no power, and the entry reports it as such.

figures.name: step9-e2-rank.svg
figures.reads: Every Bub1b genotype's percentile among 76,699 MGI genotypes under the symmetric and Phenodigm rollups. H/H and H/L1002P sit near 1% on Phenodigm, and K243R/+ leads on symmetric. The IC-matched null band spans 2.0-31.7% (symmetric) and 0.9-25.1% (Phenodigm).
figures.means: The child's terms point at Bub1b mice about ten times better than random terms of equal specificity. That supports using the hypomorph models' interventions, while the two rollups still disagree on the single best mouse.

figures.name: step9-e2-terms.svg
figures.reads: A heat map of each of the child's HPO terms against its best-matching MP term in the top Bub1b genotypes. Muscle atrophy (5.68) and failure to thrive (3.75, exact) carry the H/H match. The parental and prematurity terms match only through the mutant mice's infertility, and nephrocalcinosis scores 0 because no Bub1b genotype carries a kidney term.
figures.means: The match rests on the growth and muscle phenotypes, the same ones the D5 papers rescue. The kidney phenotype is unexplained by any mouse model.

figures.name: step9-e2-controls.svg
figures.reads: Method checks: the Bloom syndrome to Blm positive control (median 2.73% / 1.40% over 20 draws), 6 of 7 calibration diseases in the top 5%, and the other checkpoint genes' mice (Bub1 ties at 1.09%; the others 7-16%).
figures.means: The similarity method finds known disease genes, so the Bub1b result is not an artefact of the scorer.

figures.name: step9-e4-effects.svg
figures.reads: Every candidate drug in both pre-registered contrasts (rhabdomyosarcoma lines versus others; high versus low aneuploidy), grouped by direction, drawn on top of a calibration band built from 200 unrelated launched drugs put through the identical test. Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals on Cliff's delta. Only drugs measured on at least 3 in-group lines are drawn.
figures.means: The band is the point: in the 14-line rhabdomyosarcoma contrast it spans plus or minus 0.7, so only simvastatin's marker leaves it. A single drug looking selective is what this pipeline produces by chance, which is why the statin result is reported as direction-only.
figures.source: tools/render_step9_e4.py over PRISM 24Q2 and DepMap 24Q4; entry 151

figures.name: step9-e4-background.svg
figures.reads: The candidates against the whole screen. Left: the statins' percentiles among all 3,070 testable compounds. Right: dasatinib at the 99th percentile of the aneuploidy contrast, with the Mps1 and Aurora inhibitors massed at the opposite end.
figures.means: Dasatinib stands out against every compound in the screen, not just against the candidate list. The checkpoint inhibitors massing on the other side re-derive Cohen-Sharir 2021 and put a second, measured leg under the do-not table.

figures.name: step9-e4-coverage.svg
figures.reads: Which candidates the screen can actually test: the number of rhabdomyosarcoma lines each is measured on, against the 3-line minimum, with the untestable ones named.
figures.means: Ten of 24 candidates, including the report's rank-1 lead lovastatin, are below the minimum. Absence from a screen is a coverage fact, not evidence against the drug.

figures.name: step9-e56-evidence.svg
figures.reads: Candidate by source: whether the child's genome raises a question, whether his phenotypes do, both, or neither. Only drugs at least one source flags are drawn; five rows at the top are flagged by both.
figures.means: The strongest statement this step can make is a drug flagged by two independent sources. A drug flagged by neither is not safe: it means these two sources are silent about it.

figures.name: step9-e56-baserate.svg
figures.reads: The candidate set's phenotype-matched label rate (60.0%, CI 48.7-70.3) against a comparison set matched on label breadth (39.7%, CI 34.9-44.8); the intervals do not overlap.
figures.means: The candidates really do carry more of the child's own phenotypes on their labels than comparable approved drugs, so the flags are not just an artefact of drugs having long labels.

figures.name: step9-e56-coverage.svg
figures.reads: Pharmacogene positions callable from the delivered variant-only callset, per gene, against the total each gene's definition needs: 20 of 1,223 overall (1.6%), with SLCO1B1, ABCG2, CYP2C9, G6PD and UGT1A1 unreadable.
figures.means: The genomic half of the safety question cannot be answered from this delivery. That is the result, and it names the cheap fix: a targeted panel or a re-call at those positions.
